title: Burp Suite Pricing in 2026: What $499 Buys and What It Does Not
summary: Burp Suite Professional costs $499 per user a year. What Community, DAST, AI credits and Burp AT plans ($19 to $249 a month) cost, checked Nov 2026.
body_markdown:
Burp Suite Professional costs **$499 per user per year** , and the order form is unusually blunt about the “per user” part. Everyone on your team who touches it needs a seat.


That single number hides most of what you will actually spend. Community Edition is free but cannot save your work, Burp Suite DAST carries no published price at all, and Burp AI runs on a credit meter that starts with a bundle worth about five dollars.


> **What Burp Suite pricing really covers:** you are buying a named-user desktop license for manual penetration testing, not continuous coverage of an application. Automated scanning at portfolio scale sits in a separate, quote-only product, and the AI features consume a metered credit balance on top of the seat.


Below is every edition PortSwigger sells as of July 2026, what each price includes, the costs that never appear on the pricing page, and how the spend compares with[CodeAnt AI](https://www.codeant.ai/) .


## How Much Does Burp Suite Cost in 2026?

The gap between one published price and four unpublished ones is the story of Burp Suite pricing. PortSwigger sells you the tester’s seat off the shelf and negotiates everything that scales.


### Burp Suite Pro license cost and what it covers


PortSwigger's Professional page lists Burp Suite Professional at $499, and its licensing page says subscriptions are annual and per person: "Everyone who uses Burp Suite Professional needs to have a subscription." A seat cannot be shared, even if only one person uses it at a time, and users means people, not concurrent users or installations. Four testers cost $1,996 a year.


-


Terms: PortSwigger's FAQ lists 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5-year subscriptions, and the order form also offers 10 years. The only line on longer terms is "Predictable pricing when you lock in for longer." No multi-year discount is published.


-


Currencies: the order form offers US dollars, euros and British pounds. There is no rupee price list, so buyers in India pay in one of those three.


-


Adding users mid-term is charged pro rata for the days left on the licence.


-


Renewal is automatic: payment is taken 14 days before expiry from the card saved on your account.


-


Tax: PortSwigger has collected US sales tax in applicable states since December 2024, so a US invoice can come to more than $499 a seat.

## Is Burp Suite Free? Community Edition vs Professional


Burp Suite Community Edition is genuinely free and permanently available, and it deliberately withholds the features that make testing efficient. PortSwigger positions it as an “Essential manual toolkit - perfect for learning more about AppSec.”


The official comparison is the clearest statement of what the $499 upgrade buys.


Community gives you the HTTP(s) and WebSockets proxy with history, the essential tools (Repeater, Decoder, Sequencer, and Comparer), and what PortSwigger labels “Burp Intruder (demo)”.


Professional adds the seven capabilities below, each of which is a hard blocker, not a convenience.


-


**Project files.** Community holds everything in memory, so closing Burp discards your site map, history, and findings. Reopening means re-walking the application.


-


**Burp Intruder, full version.** The free build ships a demo. PortSwigger does not publish the throttle rate, so treat community reports of the exact delay as unofficial.


-


**The web vulnerability scanner.** Community has no Burp Scanner at all, which removes both crawling and auditing.


-


**Burp Collaborator.** Auto and manual out-of-band testing is Pro-only, and OAST is how blind SSRF, blind XSS, and asynchronous injection get caught.


-


**Automatic crawling and content discovery.** Free users map the application by hand.


-


**Pro-exclusive BApp extensions.** Part of the extension library requires a Pro license.


-


**Search.** Finding a string across captured traffic is a paid feature.


Community works for learning, for a one-off look at a request, and for the[Web Security Academy](https://portswigger.net/web-security) labs, which PortSwigger keeps free. Sustained professional testing without project files is impractical, because you re-map the application every time you close the window.


### Is there a free trial of Burp Suite Professional?


Yes. PortSwigger's Professional page has a "Try for free" option for a trial of the full product. The page does not state how long the trial lasts, and third-party pricing pages disagree (one says 21 days, another says there is no time-limited trial), so check the length on the trial form before you plan an evaluation around it. PortSwigger's pricing and licensing pages list no free Professional licence: the free options are Community Edition and the trial.


## How Much Does Burp Suite DAST Cost?


Burp Suite DAST pricing is quote-only in 2026, with no list price anywhere on portswigger.net. PortSwigger removed its published rate card and now routes every buyer through sales. PortSwigger's licensing page states the meter plainly: DAST comes with unlimited users, and its cost depends on how many websites you need to secure.


The[DAST pricing page](https://portswigger.net/burp/dast/pricing) states four commitments instead of numbers. Subscriptions include “no limits on the number of users”, they are “customized based on your specific requirements”, you choose “between self-hosted options or running DAST scans via PortSwigger’s secure cloud”, and scanning ranges “From ad-hoc scanning managed by the hour to unlimited scalable scanning capabilities.”


A useful commercial detail sits in the[DAST FAQs](https://portswigger.net/burp/dast/resources/faqs) rather than the pricing page. PortSwigger says “You don’t pay per URL, making it an extremely flexible solution for growing enterprises”, which distinguishes it from per-app and per-FQDN competitors.


### The name change that confuses quotes


Burp Suite Enterprise Edition became Burp Suite DAST in May 2025. PortSwigger described it as “just a new, clearer name for Burp Suite Enterprise Edition” and explained that the old name “often led to confusion, with some assuming it was merely a multi-user version of Burp Suite Professional.”


Old quotes, procurement records, and third-party pricing pages still use the Enterprise name. Match the product by capability, not by label, when you compare a 2024 renewal against a 2026 proposal.

## What Do Burp AI and Burp AT Add to the Bill?


Both are paid on top of a Professional seat.


Burp AI has two ways to pay:


-


AI credits: bought from your PortSwigger account, which must have a Burp Suite Professional licence on it. PortSwigger's documentation does not publish pack prices. Credits belong to one user, cannot be shared or pooled across a team, and expire 12 months after purchase. Light features such as Explainer use few credits; Explore Issue usually uses more. Burp checks your balance before each request and deducts afterwards, so the balance can dip below zero.


-


Burp AI subscription: an add-on to a Professional licence, billed annually and priced on team seats, with "Unrestricted usage across your team." There is no public price; PortSwigger quotes it after a demo.


Burp AT, PortSwigger's agentic AI tester, is priced separately:


-


Every paid Professional licence includes "a small Burp AT allowance each month at no additional cost." PortSwigger does not state how large it is.


-


Individual plans, each needing a Professional licence and rolling monthly: Standard $19 per user per month for occasional use, Plus $89 for about 5 times the usage of Standard, and Power $249 for about 16 times. You can change plan at any time.


-


Team and Enterprise plans are quoted on request.


-


Burp AT tasks also draw on your AI credit balance, and a higher reasoning effort setting costs more time and credits.


### The 2026 additions


PortSwigger now sells[Burp AI subscriptions](https://portswigger.net/burp/ai/subscriptions) alongside credit packs, which is the option to ask about if you would rather not track balances per person. The page describes seat-based annual pricing with unrestricted usage, and it publishes no figures, only a demo form.


Burp AT, the agentic AI product, entered public beta for Professional users in July 2026. Its billing follows the same meter, with credits “deducted as tasks progress”, and no rate card. The[Burp Suite features guide](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/burp-suite-features) covers what Burp AT and the rest of the toolkit actually do.


## What Is the Real Total Cost of Burp Suite?


The licence is the smallest line you will pay. Here is a worked example from PortSwigger's published prices, for a team of three testers who use Burp AT through the week:

What that number leaves out:


-


Tester time: the hours your testers spend scoping, testing, verifying and writing up. PortSwigger cannot price it for you, and it decides the real cost.


-


AI credits beyond the included allowance: pack prices are not published.


-


Burp Suite DAST, if you want scheduled scanning: quote only.


-


Hardware: PortSwigger recommends 2 CPU cores and 16GB of RAM as a general spec and 4 cores with 32GB for large automated scans. Each project file needs 2GB of disk and can grow to many tens of GB.


And three things no Burp line item buys:


1.


A test someone else runs and stands behind. Burp gives your tester evidence in a project file. An auditor, a bank partner or an enterprise customer usually wants a report from an outside tester.


2.


Coverage of what you did not point it at. Burp tests the targets you give it. Security leads on our calls who have used Burp Suite for years still buy a pentest because they have IP ranges, domains and APIs nobody has time to test by hand, and they want testing on their release cadence, not when a tester is free.


3.


Judgment on business logic. The OWASP Web Security Testing Guide says business logic flaws "cannot be detected by a vulnerability scanner" and that finding them "relies upon the skills and creativity of the penetration tester." Burp makes a skilled tester faster; it does not supply one.


Buying the test from a services firm has its own hidden line: most scope by the hour per domain or app, and each retest after a fix adds more hours.

CodeAnt AI has run 12,000 pentests and is trusted by more than 1,000 companies, including Fortune 500 companies like NRG, cybersecurity leaders like Commvault, and fast-growing companies like 11x and Sanas.


CodeAnt prices each pentest on the attack surface you have, and gives very generous pricing to fast-growing companies.


The two are not either-or. A team with its own testers can keep Burp for hands-on work and use a pentest for full-surface coverage and the report its auditor and customers read.


Neither model is universally better. Buy Burp Suite Professional when you have a skilled tester who needs maximum manual control over individual requests. ## Is Burp Suite Worth the Price?


Burp Suite Professional is worth $499 a seat when someone on your team tests web apps by hand most weeks. PortSwigger calls it "The world's #1 web penetration testing toolkit," and the price is small next to the tester's time. The value breaks down when:


-


**Nobody on your staff runs manual tests.** A seat you open twice a year is expensive shelfware, and an outcome-priced pentest covers the same ground without the license.


-


**You need breadth rather than depth.** Burp Professional tests what your tester points it at, so covering a portfolio continuously means buying DAST separately at an unpublished price.


-


**Your risk starts in the code.** Burp is a black-box toolkit with no source-code analysis, so anything that needs[static analysis alongside dynamic testing](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/sast-vs-dast) requires a second product.


-


Do you need a report that someone outside your team stands behind, for an auditor, a bank partner or a customer? Burp gives your tester evidence; it does not give you a third-party pentest report.


Reviewers consistently flag the same friction. G2’s summary of Burp Suite reviews cites the cost of the Professional version and occasional false positives in automated scans among the recurring complaints, alongside strong marks for the interface and real-time interception.


## Questions to Settle Before You Buy


Get written answers to these before the purchase order goes out, particularly for a DAST quote where nothing is published.


-


How many people genuinely need a seat, given that sharing one is prohibited?


-


Does the term length lock the price, and what happens at renewal?


-


For DAST, what defines scanning capacity, and how does the price move when it grows?


-


Is the deployment self-hosted or PortSwigger cloud, and what infrastructure does self-hosting require?


-


Who pays for AI credits once the initial bundle is spent, and does a subscription work out cheaper than packs?


-


What covers the application between manual engagements?


That last question is the one that decides whether a Burp license is your whole programme or one instrument in it. Comparing[continuous and annual pentesting](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/continuous-vs-annual-pentesting) models is a better next step than negotiating the seat count.


## Where This Leaves You


Burp Suite pricing is transparent exactly where the product is a desktop tool and opaque everywhere it becomes a platform. You can buy a $499 seat this afternoon without speaking to anyone, and you cannot learn what portfolio scanning costs without a sales call.


Budget the seat, then budget the tester, the hardware, the credits, and whatever covers your applications during the fifty weeks nobody is testing them. For the capability side of the decision, the[Burp Suite features breakdown](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/burp-suite-features) and the[best Burp Suite alternatives](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/burp-suite-alternatives) cover what you get and what else can do it.
